newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Cimsa aims to more than double 1997 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cimsa aims to more than double 1997 turnover.

text.p: Turkish cement and ready-mix concrete producer Cimsa Cimento Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. seeks to raise its 1997 turnover by more than 100 percent with the help of capacity expansion investments, a senior company official said.
"Our target is to raise our total sales to 21 trillion lira in 1997 from 9.418 trillion lira or $117 million in 1996," Yilmaz Kulcu, general manager of the company, told Reuters.
The company represents 5.5 percent of the total sales and production capacity in the Turkish cement industry.
Cimsa shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange traded at 14,000 lira on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's 13,250 close.

Cimsa increased its total sales by 7.5 percent in 1996 to 1.5 million tonnes over 1995, including 1.01 million tonnes produced at its southern Mersin plant and 490,000 tonnes at the central Kayseri plant. Its total yearly capacity stands at 3.3 million tonnes.
Kulcu said they set a sale target of 1.739 million tonnes for 1997, including 1.571 million tonnes of cement and 168,000 tonnes of clinker.
Cimsa exported 36,000 tonnes of grey cement, 173,000 tonnes of white cement and 152,000 tonnes of clinker last year and plans exports of 305,000, 213,000 and 68,000 tonnes, respectively in 1997.
"We planned to increase export revenues by almost 50 percent to $31 million in 1997 from $21 million last year," he added.
To boost exports, Cimsa will use joint cement storage and packaging facilities established by the Sabanci group, the major shareholder of Cimsa, in Spain and Israel last year.
"We export bulk cement to the distributer company which owns the facilities and sells it as packaged or as bulk," Kulcu said.
Industrial Sabanci conglomerate's cement division runs six plants in Turkey, including two owned by Akcansa, a joint venture with Belgian Cimenteries.
The Sabanci group constitutes about 25 percent of Turkey's total cement production capacity of 42 million tonnes.
Cimsa expanded its white cement output capacity to 420,000 tonnes from 250,000 tonnes last year to become the world's biggest white cement producing single plant.
It plans to increase further the annual white cement production capacity to 520,000 tonnes by the end of 1997.
Cimsa exports almost 50 percent of the white cement output and controls approximately 70 percent of the domestic market as one of the three producers.
The company spent 1.1 trillion lira on investments in 1996 and plans to spend another two trillion lira this year.
Kulcu is also more optimistic for 1997 market conditions:
"Annual population growth of Turkey is still at 1.7 percent level and urbanisation rate is very high, which pushes up cement consumption by around five percent every year."

Cimsa reported 6.52 trillion lira turnover in the first nine months of 1996, against 3.19 trillion lira in the same period of 1995 while its net profits declined to 610 billion lira from 746 billion lira.
